articles.title: 'I apologize to everyone my words have upset': Kylian Mbappé reacts to 'Chinese dictator' controversy
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé has apologised after comments about a meme featuring Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong sparked anger in China.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé has apologised after comments about a meme featuring Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong sparked anger in China. The controversy has also cost the French football star partnerships with three Chinese companies, while criticism of his remarks spread across Chinese social media.“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” Mbappé said in a statement Tuesday.“I apologize to everyone my words have upset," he said. "This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."Brands End Partnerships With MbappéChinese beverage company Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground announced on Tuesday that they were ending their agreements with the footballer. All three companies issued similar statements opposing “any words and actions that hurt national sentiment”.The decisions followed the circulation of a video on X that appeared to show Mbappé discussing his favourite internet meme during an interview ahead of his appearance on the French online talk show The Bridge.Asked about the meme, Mbappé described it as “a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator”.The clip then showed an edited image placing his face on the body of Mao Zedong.Football fans often jokingly portray Mbappé as a dictator in online memes because of his larger-than-life presence in the sport. However, Mao remains a sensitive historical figure in China.He led the Communist Party to victory in the Chinese civil war and founded the People's Republic of China in 1949. While many still revere him, his rule also included disastrous policies, including the Great Leap Forward, which contributed to a famine that killed an estimated 30 million people.Social media backlash growsChina's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun also commented on the controversy, saying that “words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”Social media platform RedNote said its content partnership with Mbappé had ended on December 31, 2024, and announced it would “remove related promotional materials.” His account was also blocked from gaining new followers.Meanwhile, hashtags calling for boycotts and reporting the brands' decisions topped Weibo's trending charts, with some users criticising Mbappé and urging him not to visit China.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Javi Casquero: "Mou intervino por fin, pero ahora debe mantener la apuesta"
articles.standfirst: 'El Corrillo' es el tiempo de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.summary: 'El Corrillo' es el tiempo de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.body: Javi Casquero, Javi Tintó, David Sánchez Cañete y José Luis San Martín debaten sobre la actualidad deportiva en 'El Corrillo' de Directo MARCA junto a Rafa Sahuquillo. La tertulia de 'El Corrillo', en Radio MARCA, dejó contundentes reflexiones sobre el impacto de José Mourinho en el Real Madrid y el debate generado por el Balón de Oro. Javi Casquero no dudó en elogiar al técnico tras la victoria ante el Barcelona: "Mourinho le dio un baño táctico a Flick, y no pasa nada". El exfutbolista destacó la capacidad del entrenador para convencer a sus jugadores de asumir tareas defensivas y sacrificar protagonismo individual por el colectivo. También puso el foco en Kylian Mbappé: "Fue el primer partido que le he visto trabajar en el Real Madrid, en dos años y medio". El debate también dejó críticas a las campañas públicas de algunos aspirantes al Balón de Oro. Uno de los tertulianos cuestionó la actitud de Lamine Yamal y Mbappé tras la gala: "El Balón de Oro hay que ganárselo en el campo y no en las ruedas de prensa". En cambio, Harry Kane recibió elogios por su sencillez, su trayectoria y sus goles. David Sánchez Cañete defendió que el reconocimiento premia "la sencillez, la naturalidad, el trabajo, el esfuerzo y la constancia", mientras Casquero destacó el perfil del delantero inglés, al que comparó con Karim Benzema por su capacidad para asociarse, generar juego y marcar diferencias en ataque. La tertulia también abrió el debate sobre la gestión de Mourinho y la competencia interna en el Real Madrid. Casquero reclamó continuidad para el planteamiento colectivo mostrado ante el Barça, mientras otro de los participantes comparó la situación actual con la etapa de Xabi Alonso: "Todo lo que no le dejaron hacer a Xabi Alonso lo está haciendo Mourinho ahora". El foco se trasladó finalmente a Vinicius, que tendrá que competir por su puesto con Diomande. Casquero fue tajante: «Ningún equipo en el mundo se puede permitir dos futbolistas que no corran». Un mensaje que resume el nuevo desafío del brasileño: recuperar su mejor versión y adaptarse a las exigencias de un Madrid en el que, al menos por ahora, el rendimiento colectivo marca el camino.

articles.title: Kamario Taylor Out for Season, Latest Rumors on Mississippi State QB's Toe Injury
articles.summary: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.

Taylor addressed the situation in a statement, expressing "I love this team" and his commitment to it "won't change":

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported the sophomore could undergo surgery on his injured toe as early as Wednesday.

Taylor turned heads when the Bulldogs won their first four games. He threw for 1,192 yards and 14 touchdowns to two interceptions during that stretch.

In mid-September, The Athletic's Bruce Feldman spoke to one Big Ten coach who called Taylor "the best QB I've seen in college football in a few years."

The 6'4" signal-caller was injured in the victory over Missouri, though, and that preceded his uneven showing in a 56-23 blowout loss to Alabama. He was sidelined for the 31-0 shutout to LSU two weeks later and unsuccessfully tried to return against Oklahoma. He exited early as Mississippi State suffered a third straight defeat.

Coach Jeff Lebby was unable to provide much insight on Taylor's status during a press conference Monday.

"We're still in the process of looking at everything," he told reporters . "He is doing good. His spirits are good, but as we continue to move forward, I think we'll know a lot more here in the next 48 hours."

Needless to say, being without Taylor is a massive blow for the offense, and simply qualifying for a bowl isn't guaranteed. Mississippi State will be a big favorite over Tennessee Tech on Nov. 21 but need to take down one of No. 11 Texas, Vanderbilt, Auburn or No. 12 Ole Miss in order to get to at least six wins.

Lebby will be counting on Parker Puckett to lead the offense over the final month.

articles.title: El Cuti está de vuelta
articles.standfirst: El central argentino empieza a trabajar con el grupo, poniendo su mirada en el Levante... y sobre todo en la semana siguiente en la que el Bayern y el Barcelona visitan el Metropolitano
articles.summary: El central argentino empieza a trabajar con el grupo, poniendo su mirada en el Levante... y sobre todo en la semana siguiente en la que el Bayern y el Barcelona visitan el Metropolitano
articles.body: El Atlético volvió al trabajo en la tarde de este martes con la mejor noticia posible: el Cuti Romero está de vuelta, empezando así su cuenta atrás hacia su reaparición para comandar a una defensa que ha recuperado la fiabilidad con su presencia. Aunque el Cuti sólo realizó la primera parte del entrenamiento junto al grupo, su recuperación marcha sobre los plazos previstos, albergándose la esperanza, tal y como informó MARCA tras conocerse la lesión que se produjo en el aductor frente al Espanyol, de que pueda estar listo para visitar al Levante el sábado... y sobre todo en la siguiente semana, en la que el Bayern y Barcelona se suceden por el Metropolitano en un plazo de cinco días. En este sentido, el central argentino completaría la segunda parte de la sesión en solitario en un campo anexo, bajo la mirada de un Simeone que también dejaría al grupo para seguir atentamente sus evoluciones y comprobar que 'superaba' la prueba. No sería el único en todo caso que tendría un trabajo personalizado, pues Julián Alvarez, Kang-in, Pubill y Hancko (más tarde sería el turno de Barrios, Giuliano, Lookman y Jonathan David) realizarían carrera continua alrededor del campo en el que Cuti hacía sus ejercicios con arrancadas, pases en corto, golpeos... Pese a que en su caso su reaparición en el Ciutat de Valencia aún se antoja prematura, Koke y Cardoso también empezaron a asomar en el verde, trabajando por separado en el mismo campo que el Cuti. Así, el capitán, acompañado de Óscar Pitillas, tocaría balón, haría cambios de ritmo y esprints evidenciando que la próxima semana podría incorporarse al grupo. Cardoso, en su caso bajo las directrices de Zahínos, se limitaría a realizar ejercicios de carrera, evitando de momento los golpeos.

articles.title: Granit Xhaka: Switzerland captain and striker Breel Embolo permitted to return to national team
articles.summary: Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo will be allowed to return to action for Switzerland next month following an investigation into forged Covid-19 vaccination certificates.
articles.body:
Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo will both be allowed to play for Switzerland again next month following an investigation into forged Covid-19 vaccination certificates obtained by the pair.

Switzerland captain Xhaka missed Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia during the October international break after admitting to acquiring a fake certificate which allowed him to travel and compete in 2022.

Striker Embolo, 29, was also dropped from the Switzerland squad in September for the same reason.

The Swiss Football Association (SFV) confirmed on Tuesday that 34-year-old Sunderland midfielder Xhaka and Embolo will both be available for inclusion by manager Murat Yakin for November's fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland.

National team director Pierluigi Tami said: "We considered this from various perspectives. The specific circumstances of both cases, the concluded legal proceedings, and the sporting consequences already implemented all factored into the decision.

"We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is responsible and the right thing to do."

Both Xhaka and Embolo were fined 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) , suspended for two years provided no further offences are committed.

Xhaka, who took responsibility for his actions, has not been stripped of the captaincy.

However, the SFV said in its statement that the final decision over the captaincy remains with the team's coach, Yakin, who will announce his squad on 5 November.

Switzerland are top of Group E heading into their final two Nations League fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland on 13 and 16 November.

articles.title: Where are Celtic & Martin O'Neill a year after Brendan Rodgers exit?
articles.summary: How should Martin O'Neill and Celtic be assessed a year since his arrival in place of Brendan Rodgers as manager?
articles.body:
One year ago, Brendan Rodgers resigned as Celtic manager, with Martin O'Neill immediately taking the reigns in what the Scottish champions thought would be an interim period in charge.

Twelve months on, O'Neill is still there, albeit over two spells with 33 dismal days under Wilfried Nancy squeezed in between.

So where are Celtic at in terms of "moving forward", that cliched business term that has seeped into football parlance?

Shortly before his exit, Rodgers described the Celtic squad as "a Honda Civic rather than a Ferrari" as he bemoaned transfer spending, but how much longer will it be steered by his 74-year-old successor?

O'Neill on Johnston injury, Celtic milestone & No.1 battle

O'Neill had admitted he considered his position during the last international break, but he showed no signs of being ready to walk away when addressing the media before Wednesday's meeting with Dundee United.

Asked how he looked back on his latest year in charge, he replied: "Obviously with a lot of satisfaction and secretly probably delighted to get the call and happy with the results since. So it feels like a long year. Very long.

"The club has done more for me than I've done for the club in that sense. Seriously, it's rejuvenated me in many aspects."

Previous to his return, O'Neill had been "semi-enjoying my life watching the game from afar" and "talking nonsense most of the time" as a football pundit.

However, he was delighted with the opportunity to return to "a game that I absolutely love, will love forever".

One year of O'Neill - saviour or sticking plaster?

Rodgers' second two-year spell as Celtic manager came to an end after a 3-1 defeat at Hearts that left his side eight points behind the Edinburgh side after nine games.

They had lost two of those nine, scoring 12 goals for the loss of eight.

Despite Hearts retaining their lead until the final day of the season, Rodgers' fellow Northern Irishman would turn it round in the end with a dramatic victory over their title rivals at Celtic Park to secure their 56th league title and fifth in a row.

This season, O'Neill's side have lost only one of their 10 league games, scoring 25 times for the concession of six, to lead Rangers in the title race.

On the surface, 16 wins in 17 league games since the closing stages of last season looks like progress.

As Celtic podcaster Tino Callaghan told the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast: "On the last day of the season - 16 May - everything did turn out fine and dandy.

"Currently, things are six out of 10 at Celtic. We're four points clear at the top of the league this week's midweek card can see us extend that lead, but things are far from correct in terms of the evolution of the club and the progress of the club."

O'Neill's win percentage of nearly 75% in his latest spell is similar to his club record level during his trophy-laden five years in charge to 2005.

However, the recent 7-1 thrashing of Hearts apart, performances this season have largely left the Celtic support underwhelmed, while it is results in Europe - and two defeats in a week by city rivals Rangers - that have caused most alarm.

When Rodgers left, Celtic had won eight games, drawn four and lost four overall at the start of last season.

This season, they have won 11 and lost six, but on their way to a Champions League exit and to the foot of the Europa League after three games, they have suffered heavy defeats against LASK, Ferencvaros and Benfica.

"O'Neill domestically is more than capable," Callaghan said. "But the Celtic squad is woefully inept when it comes to European football and you just need to have a glance at that for evidence when you look at the bench on those European nights."

That led former Celtic striker Chris Sutton to describe the side currently under his former manager as flat-track bullies only able to dominate in Scottish football.

"We're just falling way, way behind," Callaghan agreed. "But it wasn't that long ago where we were competing with Bayern Munich and beating Leipzig and pulling off some really decent results."

Last season was also marked by a damaging split between the board and sections of the support unhappy at the level of investment in the squad and the general running of the club.

The two sides united for last season's victorious climax to the season, but the splits have re-emerged.

"Ultimately it always comes down to recruitment, doesn't it?" Callaghan said. "I hear folks talking about entitled Celtic fans, but millions of pounds in the bank is no use unless you're spending it.

"It's about spending more effectively and it's spending certainly more efficiently and sooner within the window.

"The start of the window was exciting. Camilo Duran is a brilliant player. As good a signing as we've made in some time, Mika Baur the same.

"But the defensive midfield has been a serious issue. We haven't signed anyone there and you're now starting to feel sorry for Callum McGregor - he's been hung out to dry."

Daily Record football writer Michael Gannon agreed that O'Neill had been used as a human shield by the board.

"I feel for him a little bit because he's the only person at Celtic who fronts up and faces questions on a regular basis," he said.

"A lot of the questions, like where is the full-time chairman, where's the head of recruitment, where's the director of football, what's happened with the Green Brigade bans and fan problems, are not really for him to answer."

Callaghan appears to speak for many fans for whom O'Neill still feels like a stop-gap "holding position for all concerned".

"But, within that year, he's won a league and he's won a Scottish Cup as well, so not too bad," he said.

"I don't see him staying beyond this year. I think from his point of view, European football at Celtic became a thing again under O'Neill and I do think part of his decision-making in the summer to return will have been the prospect of a final chance at the Champions League, final crack at the big time.

"And he'll have been as devastated as anyone that we fell short against LASK. And I do think there's still a bit of a hangover amongst the players from that one."

After a poor start to the Europa League, will O'Neill now make finishing on a high domestically his priority?

"He will be conscious of his legacy whether he says so or otherwise and I think, whatever happens, he'll want to certainly move on this summer, if that is the case, with another league title under his belt," Gallacher added.

Club rudderless and outdated? - the fans' view

Michael: Rodgers appears somewhat vindicated. Since leaving, the board have proven their lack of direction and the resulting diminished quality largely confirmed what we all suspected. That the club is rudderless and outdated. Rodgers was the chewing gum holding the straw tower up.

Johnno: As time moves on, it appears that Celtic don't. The team has not improved since Rodgers engineered his exit. Had the board kept faith with O'Neill last year instead of appointing Nancy at the worst possible time, there would have been no final-day drama. However, last season appears to have drained whatever team spirit, confidence and cohesion was left. This season has been a mixture of underwhelming performances, dreadful tactics and utter chaos in defence.

Brian: The last year has proven the board are not fit for purpose and have absolutely no idea how to run a modern football club. The club is going backwards with the future looking increasingly dim.

Frank: Two out of the three major trophies cannot be bad and Europe can be an irritating sideshow to the quest for the championship. To only have lost one game in the league is very commendable.

Paul: Rodgers' departure was symptomatic of our current demise. The performance v Bayern in Feb '25 was an aberration and disguised a lot of the flaws that, even then, Rodgers was aware of. Can't blame him for leaving as the fish had been rotting for a while by then and we all know where that rot begins.

Nick: I feel we were very fortunate to win the league last year. Hearts and Rangers fell away badly at the end. I don't think O'Neill should have stayed in charge as he hasn't really achieved much since leaving in 2005. There is no style, no direction and little optimism from what I see with a very disgruntled fan base and a board that lacks vision.

articles.title: Arsene Wenger's 'daylight' offside goal trial unlikely to be extended over lack of Ifab support
articles.summary: Arsene Wenger's "daylight" offside trial is unlikely to be extended after receiving a lack of support at the Ifab assessment panels.
articles.body:
Arsene Wenger's "daylight" offside trial is unlikely to be extended after receiving a lack of support at the International Football Association Board's (Ifab) assessment panels on Tuesday.

The trial, which sees a player ruled to be onside if any part of the body is level with the second-last opponent, has been operating in the Canadian Premier League (CPL) throughout the year.

The regular CPL season finished on Sunday, with mixed results.

The Ifab's football and technical panels, made up of former players, coaches and referees, were told that the trial had led to a 54% reduction in offside decisions and 13 additional goals across the 112 matches.

But it also resulted in the defensive line retreating three metres across the course of the season.

The CPL also trialled Football Video Support - a version of VAR which allows coaches to challenge decisions twice a game.

This helped limit the impact of the trial, which would not be possible in most leagues.

The biggest impact appeared to be on set-pieces, with defences having to compensate for the advantage of the "daylight" offside.

There was support for a change to the coin toss before a penalty shootout.

At present there is a toss to decide which end a penalty is taken from, and then a captain makes a call for choice of first spot-kick.

It means the same team can get the advantage of both decisions on a shootout.

The planned change would see the captain who wins the toss the choice of ends or first kick, with the opposition skipper automatically getting to decide the other.

There was little support for extending the five-second countdown for throw-ins and goal-kicks to other situations such as free-kicks and corners.

The goalkeeper injury trial currently being using in English football was viewed as a success so far.

This sees an outfield player leave the field of play if a goalkeeper goes down for treatment, to try to end the tactical timeout which had become prevalent.

It has only been enforced twice in 80 Premier League games so far.

One suggestion was a player who claims a head injury in the penalty area and gets up quickly after the referee stops play should not have up stay off the field for one minute.

The technical panels meetings on Tuesday were the first step to potential law changes for the 2027-28 season.

Footballs lawmakers are eager not to make too many changes after so many modifications in the summer ahead of the World Cup.

articles.title: De eliminar al Real Madrid a la dura realidad de la lucha por la supervivencia
articles.standfirst: Un año después de una Copa histórica, el Alba afronta otra edición en un contexto muy distinto
articles.summary: Un año después de una Copa histórica, el Alba afronta otra edición en un contexto muy distinto
articles.body: Hace un año, la Copa del Rey fue la gran alegría de la temporada del Albacete Balompié. Este miércoles vuelve a asomar el torneo copero en el calendario, pero lo hace en circunstancias completamente distintas. El conjunto manchego visita al Calvo Sotelo Puertollano, equipo de Segunda RFEF, en la primera ronda del torneo del K.O., pero lo hace como colista de Segunda división, con cuatro puntos tras once jornadas, aunque llega después de lograr ante el Eldense su primera victoria del curso. Es inevitable que la mirada se desvíe hacia el próximo partido de Liga, también en el Carlos Belmonte, frente al Sabadell, una cita que todo el entorno considera de vital importancia, pero la Copa está otra vez aquí y reclama su protagonismo. La memoria sigue muy viva. El curso pasado el Alba eliminó al San Fernando canario, al Leganés y, en la tanda de penaltis, al Celta, antes de protagonizar la gran noche del Belmonte: el 3-2 al Real Madrid del debutante Arbeloa en octavos, con doblete de Jefté Betancor y gol de Javi Villar, en el que fue su primer triunfo ante el conjunto blanco. La aventura terminó con honor en cuartos, con una derrota por 1-2 ante el Barcelona con un Carlos Belmonte lleno y con un gol de Javi Moreno que hizo creer en otra hazaña. Fue mucho más que un éxito deportivo: la Copa, con la visita de tres equipos de Primera división en un mismo curso, convirtió a la capital manchega en el epicentro del fútbol nacional durante semanas y supuso una importante inyección económica para el club y la ciudad. Ese recuerdo explica que Joseba Etxeberria quiera tomarse el torneo con total seriedad sin perder de vista dónde se juega el Alba su futuro. El técnico lo dejó claro en la rueda de prensa previa: “Queremos seguir en la Copa, queremos ganar mañana y estar en el próximo sorteo. Evidentemente cuando tienes que jugar domingo, miércoles y sábado tienes que rotar, pero tenemos gente preparada que está trabajando en el día a día muy bien”. Y también ve la competición como una oportunidad para reforzar la confianza de un equipo necesitado: “Estamos en una situación muy delicada y necesitamos todo tipo de noticias positivas y volver a ganar sería la mejor noticia”. Su reflexión conecta ambas competiciones: “Creo que también el hecho de poder pasar mañana en Copa nos va a influir para el sábado, porque al final el equipo va a ir cogiendo seguridad, va a hacer que a la gente le apetezca más ir al Belmonte el sábado”. Esté en juego la Copa o la Liga el técnico de Elgoibar tiene claro el mensaje a sus futbolistas: “El que esté jugando con continuidad y baje un poco su rendimiento va a ir fuera y el que está tocando a la puerta de la titularidad va a jugar. A mí me da igual la edad, la experiencia, la madurez. Son pequeños condicionantes pero el condicionante que va a marcar todo es el rendimiento”. Su mensaje final no admite dudas sobre las prioridades: “Luego ya pensaremos en el Sabadell sabiendo que nuestra situación en Liga es muy delicada, pero vamos a ir partido a partido y lo que ahora toca es la Copa”. Qué le deparará la Copa a este Alba tan necesitado es una incógnita, pero la mirada al pasado más reciente resulta inevitable: el recuerdo de aquellas semanas mágicas sigue en la retina de una afición que atraviesa un inicio de temporada muy duro.

articles.title: Jadon Sancho descarta fichar por el Getafe al tener una oferta millonaria
articles.standfirst: El futbolista británico pedía tres millones de euros netos hasta final de temporada y el club azulón no podía llegar a esa cifra
articles.summary: El futbolista británico pedía tres millones de euros netos hasta final de temporada y el club azulón no podía llegar a esa cifra
articles.body: El sueño del Getafe de fichar a Jadon Sancho se ha esfumado. El extremo británico comunicó a Ángel Torres que no jugará en el conjunto azulón al tener una millonaria oferta del fútbol árabe. Jadon Sancho pedía tres millones de euros netos hasta final de temporada para fichar por un Getafe que tenía mucho interés por reforzarse con un extremo, petición de Bordalás para mejorar los recursos de una plantilla muy escasa para tres competiciones. Pese a que en Inglaterra hablaron de una oferta de 400.000 euros, el club azulón puso bastante más dinero encima de la mesa, pero lejos de las pretensiones del jugador inglés. Los agentes del exfutbolista del Manchester United, Aston Villa, Chelsea y Dortmund están cerrando la operación y en la mañana de este martes han desechado la opción de jugar en LaLiga y fichar por el Getafe. Su destino apunta al fútbol árabe, donde están dispuestos a pagar lo que pide Jadon Sancho, que estaría por encima de lo que solicitaban al Getafe al tener que salir de Europa. El cuadro de Bordalás, que tiene dos fichas libres, da por cerrado el capítulo de fichajes hasta que se abra el mercado de invierno el próximo 2 de enero salvo que aparezca algo muy interesante. Este martes ha visitado las oficinas del Coliseum el presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas, dentro de un clima de concordia con el máximo dirigente azulón, Ángel Torres. "Las relaciones son inmejorables", ha afirmado el presidente. Más enfadado estaba el mandatario del Getafe con la Federación, ya que considera evitable que el Sevilla y el Betis jueguen contra equipos madrileños (Sporting Hortaleza y Navalcarnero) mientras que Getafe y Rayo tienen que viajar a Andalucía (Lebrija y Huelva). "Nos va a costar 60.000 euros este partido", afirmó Torres.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Responds to Rumors He Offered $50K to Have People Not Criticize Him
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders has responded to a rumor about him offering $50,000 to people if they didn't criticize him.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders has responded to a rumor about him offering $50,000 to people if they didn't criticize him.

Asked about the rumor during his Tuesday press conference, Sanders clarified the offer was intended as a joke to see how long they the media could go without mentioning his name.

The question came about after Christopher Neely, who has served as Sanders' personal videographer, said in an interview that Coach Prime extended a cash offer to his critics to see if they would not say anything negative about him in public:

"For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack. Which is why he told some of them, 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."

He later addressed the "lie" on social media:

Sanders has been one of the most high-profile figures in all of college football since 2020 when he was hired as the head coach at Jackson State.

The spotlight got even brighter on Sanders when he took over Colorado prior to the 2023 season, particularly after Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter joined him in Boulder.

After the Buffaloes started 3-0 in Sanders' first season, they lost eight of their final nine games. They rebounded in 2024 with a 9-4 record, their most wins in a season since 2016.

Hunter won the Heisman Trophy, joining Rashaan Salaam as the only Colorado players who have received the honor.

Since that time, though, Colorado has a 5-14 record under Sanders. The team is off to a 2-5 start so far in 2026, including an 0-4 record in Big 12 play. The Buffaloes are the only Big 12 team without a conference victory.

They have lost three of their four Big 12 games by at least 10 points, with a 57-24 loss to Oklahoma State in their most recent contest.

Sanders is in the second season of a five-year, $54 million extension he signed with Colorado in March 2025 that runs through 2029. He is currently the 14th-highest-paid head coach in FBS.

articles.title: Harry Kane: How the ‘runt of the litter’ conquered a historic Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Once mocked for being the most famous player never to win a trophy, Kane now has the most prestigious individual honour.
articles.body:
Gently planting a kiss on the Ballon d’Or trophy , Harry Kane proudly lifted the shiny silverware into the air with a look of disbelief on his face.

The cameras flashed, the “home” crowd erupted in thunderous applause, and an unassuming winner basked in his moment of glory.

Hundreds of England fans had lined up outside the London Palladium for this moment, while millions more across the country had waited for it with bated breath. It was a day 25 years in the making.

For Kane, it was an achievement beyond belief and a victory too bold to dream of.

Monday’s hometown glory was Kane’s crowning moment – a testament to his remarkable talent and sheer consistency.

He was never the superstar – far from it. For years, he struggled for game time. Loaned from one club to another. Not a teenage prodigy. Not one to watch out for.

But that never deterred the boy from Leytonstone, who, year after year, put in the hard work and silenced the outside noise. Now, at 33 years old, when many of his peers are past their prime, Kane is peaking at the perfect time.

Often mocked for not winning trophies, Kane – it seemed – was busy making space for the ultimate prize: the Ballon d’Or – football’s most prestigious individual honour .

“Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn’t have thought I’d be this far,” Kane told DAZN.

“I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now,” he added.

“I had to bide my time and work hard; a lot of times it was me against my own mind, and I had to come through it. I had to show self-belief, determination. I think that grounded me, even when I did make it at the highest level, to keep improving and keep getting better.”

Hardships have been a constant in Kane’s career, right from his early days in football.

At eight years old, Kane joined the Arsenal academy. But that didn’t last long. Labelled “a bit chubby” and “not very athletic” by then academy director Liam Brady, the forward was released after just one season.

It was a move that baffled veteran French manager Arsene Wenger – who managed Arsenal for more than two decades – when he discovered the news years later.

By 13, Kane was on the development programme at Tottenham Hotspur. Academy director John McDermott described him as the “runt of the litter”, saying Kane was heavily lagging behind his peers.

“He was not fast. He was the runt of the litter – 30 percent down on the rest of the group!” McDermott said in a 2016 interview with Goal.

It took Tottenham a bit of convincing before Kane got his shot at senior football in 2009. But that wasn’t very smooth sailing either. Kane endured loan spells across the English football pyramid, including Leyton Orient, Millwall, Leicester City, and Norwich City.

There were almost two years between Kane’s first Spurs goal, against Shamrock Rovers in 2011, and his next, against Hull City in 2013.

Even after his breakthrough season in 2014-15, Kane was dubbed a “one-season wonder”.

An incredible 19-year spell at Spurs shaped Kane into the player he is today.

During his 14 senior seasons at the North London club, Kane ticked off records that once seemed unbelievable to his younger self – three Premier League Golden Boots, six PFA Premier League Team of the Year nominations, and a club-record 280 goals in more than 430 appearances in all competitions.

But for all his individual brilliance and long-lasting impact, Kane walked away with no major trophies.

He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and was in English teams that twice lost the European Championship final.

For most of his career, the football world saw him as the most famous player never to win a trophy.

Kane waited until he was 31 years old to lift his first silverware – the 2024-25 Bundesliga title with Bayern Munich.

Since then, the England international has added four more club trophies, including another German top-flight title and the German Cup.

Kane’s trophy collection does not do justice to his individual brilliance .

A lethal striker in all senses, he is England’s record scorer with 91, the highest-scoring English player in the Champions League (58) and the second-highest scorer in the Premier League (213).

Last month, he also became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, hitting the landmark on his 98th league appearance for Bayern.

Kane’s sublime finishing is not his only talent. Honing an instinct he first developed as a youth team player, Kane has also blossomed into a gifted playmaker.

“I feel like I’ve always had the passing range and the vision and the football brain – the game understanding – throughout my whole career, and I think that’s just flourished these last couple of years,” he told UEFA.com.

It would be safe to say Kane, arguably the best English player of his generation, is improving with age.

His staggering 73 goals across club and country last season were the most by a footballer since Lionel Messi’s haul of 82 in 2011-12.

Unlike Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, who both won the World Cup as teenagers, Kane did not appear destined for greatness. But on Monday, he proved the doubters wrong, ending England’s 25-year wait for a Ballon d’Or winner.

He didn’t need a mega publicity campaign like Yamal or Mbappe , who dominated headlines in the build-up to the award ceremony. Kane let his football do the talking.

It is little wonder, then, that Kane has been posting nonstop on his social media accounts the morning after his Ballon d’Or triumph. He simply can’t get enough of it.

After all, the young boy whom no one believed in is today standing tall as the world’s best footballer.

articles.title: Michael Carrick: Why Man Utd are sticking with under-pressure manager - for now
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at the 48 hours that led to Manchester United deciding to keep under-pressure Michael Carrick as their head coach for Saturday's trip to Chelsea.
articles.body:
When Michael Carrick disappeared down the tunnel after Manchester United's loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday, the support from fans for a legendary player turned to hostility and anger at the current squad.

The atmosphere afterwards was said to be emotional.

Carrick was the last to leave the stadium and, as usual, patiently posed for selfies and signed shirts for the fans who remained on what had been a foul day weather-wise, and an awful one on the pitch.

Asked in his post-match news conference if he expected to be in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea, Carrick said: "I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I'm carrying on as normal."

Few felt that was sustainable. Even Carrick's coaching team wondered whether they would survive.

United have decided Carrick and his players will have the chance to turn the present situation around. No timescale has been put on this, but Carrick will be in charge at Chelsea, with his team 16th in the table.

They have a crucial Champions League match against Roma three days later, then a Premier League encounter with in-form Aston Villa before a two-week international break.

No-one from Manchester United is saying so, but that would be the most obvious time to decide if a change of coach is required.

On Monday morning, when it was widely anticipated an announcement terminating Carrick's tenure would be made, a senior figure at United said calmness and a clear head would be needed to navigate the turbulence around Old Trafford.

Carrick had been treading water since the crushing 4-1 defeat at Como on 21 October - one of the worst European nights in club history.

Respected United fan and United We Stand fanzine editor Andy Mitten, who interviewed chief executive Omar Berrada on behalf of the club last June, described the performance as "an affront to the name of Manchester United".

In addition to the catastrophic nature of the performance, captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick's tactics and the inability of his coaches to spot what was going wrong.

Fernandes' comments came a week after defender Lisandro Martinez said he had expected more investment in the squad and - turning attention to Jason Wilcox - "more from our technical director".

It painted a picture of a squad out of control, posing an immediate dilemma for the United hierarchy.

Feeling it would look reactionary and impulsive to remove Carrick based on the negativity of one game, United stuck with the 45-year-old for the Bournemouth match - only for that to turn sour thanks to a performance that, arguably, was worse than the one in Italy.

Fernandes played no part and was dropped to the bench. Afterwards, the Portugal star liked an Instagram post which included the caption: "Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care".

Late on Sunday night, BBC Sport was led to believe a final decision to sack Carrick had not been made, and the judgement would stretch into Monday.

There was no decision then, either. The United players who started against Bournemouth were given the day off but bizarrely, Fernandes and Carrick were both at Carrington. Fernandes was having pre-planned treatment while Carrick watched a closed doors Under-21s game.

Also at the training ground were Berrada and Wilcox, discussing what the immediate future should look like. Sources say it is inconceivable minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family would not have been part of those discussions.

It was early evening before it became clear there would be no update on Carrick's future. His arrival at Carrington at 07:30 GMT on Tuesday was a sign he would take training as normal and, along with Fernandes and several other players, Carrick signed autographs and posed for photographs with a group of fans invited to the training ground that day.

Four hours later, United sources confirmed he would be in charge at Stamford Bridge.

The current predicament at the club is seen as not being entirely Carrick's fault.

Senior figures at the club feel United's players - a squad they think are capable of qualifying for the Champions League - are underperforming badly and should shoulder some of the blame.

There does seem to be a general desire to help Carrick out. One player told BBC Sport: "The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone."

It is not known if the "we" includes Fernandes, and BBC Sport has not been made aware of what, if any, conversations have taken place between the captain and his boss.

Obviously, it is easier to get rid of one manager and his backroom team than an entire squad of players - and if results do not turn around, Carrick will pay the price.

One former senior United official told BBC Sport: "Ordinarily, Michael would have gone. The last two performances were unacceptable and team discipline is broken. Not doing it is fascinating and risky."

Cynics may argue the main reason Carrick is still in a job is because of the inability to secure a replacement before the Chelsea game. Additionally, some of the coaches current Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher called on to help him during his spell as interim manager in January are now part of the senior set-up.

As highlighted by BBC Sport on Monday, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann were among the options explored by United as they weighed up whether to make a change. Any decision to appoint Howe would trigger a multi-million pound compensation payment from his former club Newcastle. Some observers think compensation payments may be a factor in United's reluctance to make a change, given the sums that have previously gone on hiring and firing coaches.

BBC Sport has also been told former Chelsea boss Antonio Conte is willing to have a conversation about the job, although there has been no direct contact.

That trio are all out of work - as is Kieran McKenna, who worked with Carrick as part of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's coaching team at United and then left for Ipswich.

Aston Villa's Unai Emery also has strong backing at United, but the club are realistic about their chances of tempting the Spaniard from Villa Park.

Wilcox's future has also come under intense scrutiny.

One source close to United feels it is inevitable the former Blackburn and Leeds player will eventually lose his job if a third managerial change in as many seasons is made.

There is sympathy with Wilcox, who did not set the summer transfer budget. Others say Ratcliffe has provided significant funds for transfers since he took charge of football affairs in early 2024, as well as injecting £300m of his own money into the club.

While disgruntled fans may point to the recruitment of teams such as Brentford and Brighton as proof good players can be signed without paying astronomical fees, options for bigger clubs such as United were said to be scarce during the summer window.

Nevertheless, it has never been explained why it was decided to focus on bolstering the midfield last summer, rather than address clear personnel issues at left-back and central striker. Injuries to Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko have made that issue even more acute.

Another senior figure in the game told BBC Sport both Wilcox and Berrada may be vulnerable, suggesting Ratcliffe could be considering a wider overhaul of senior staff.

For now, though, minds are focused on Stamford Bridge, with Carrick due to speak to the media on Thursday.

articles.title: Bob Chesney 'Very Excited' About UCLA Future amid Speculation He Could Leave for Other CFB Jobs
articles.summary: With UCLA far exceeding expectations on the field, coach Bob Chesney is already having to ease the anxieties of fans who think he could leave for a bigger job.
articles.body:
With UCLA far exceeding expectations on the field, coach Bob Chesney is already having to ease the anxieties of fans who think he could leave for a bigger job.

Chesney told reporters Tuesday he's "truly" enjoying his time in L.A. and is "very excited" about the long-term direction of the program:

The Bruins appear to have hit a home run with the 49-year-old, who went 21-6 in his two seasons as the head coach at James Madison. Those across the country in Happy Valley are certainly looking longingly at what could've been .

The general state of college football is reflected by the fact Chesney even has to be asked about his UCLA future when he's just seven games into his tenure.

Lincoln Riley swapped Oklahoma for USC. Lane Kiffin bolted Ole Miss for LSU as the Rebels were primed to qualify for the College Football Playoff. Kalen DeBoer took the Alabama job less than a week after coaching Washington in the national championship.

There are a lot of factors working in UCLA's factor. It's located in one of the world's biggest media markets. There's a ton of high school talent within the state. The Rose Bowl is among the most recognizable venues in the sport. And there's the benefit of playing in the Big Ten.

The Bruins have the ingredients needed to be a consistent winner.

Still, there are other schools that have more history, better resources or a combination of the two. You probably can't take the NFL totally off the table, either, when coaching in the pros has become less stressful than the year-round grind of leading a college program.

It's too soon to think Chesney will actually leave, but he'll likely get a lucrative new extension , which on its own would illustrate how UCLA can't take anything for granted while trying to keep him in Westwood.

articles.title: Tebas se reúne con el embajador de China en España: "Buscamos soluciones para superar este episodio"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de LaLiga hace pública una imagen del encuentro
articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga hace pública una imagen del encuentro
articles.body: Javier Tebas dio este martes otro paso más en su intención de enfriar la polémica creada por la repercusión que han tenido en China las declaraciones de Kylian Mbappé. El presidente de LaLiga, que horas antes ya pidió disculpas al pueblo chino tanto con con un mensaje en su cuenta de X como con un comunicado en la web de LaLiga, publicó un mensaje posterior, acompañado de una foto, de la reunión suya con el embajador de China en España. En su mensaje, Tebas también desgrana de manera detallada muchos de los acuerdos de colaboración que LaLiga mantiene con el gigante asiático. Hoy he mantenido una reunión con el embajador de China en España para abordar la situación generada por las declaraciones de Kylian Mbappé y buscar soluciones que permitan superar este episodio. Durante los últimos años, desde LALIGA hemos trabajado mano a mano con las autoridades chinas, las instituciones del fútbol, los operadores audiovisuales y las empresas del país para impulsar el crecimiento y la popularidad del fútbol español en China, pero también para contribuir al desarrollo y crecimiento del propio fútbol chino, compartiendo nuestra experiencia, conocimientos y recursos. Queremos que nuestros acuerdos de colaboración, especialmente el convenio estratégico con la Chinese Professional Football League (CFL), vigente hasta 2029, y los acuerdos con China Media Group (CMG), entre otros proyectos conjuntos, sigan siendo un éxito y contribuyan tanto a hacer cada vez más grande el fútbol chino como a acercar nuestras competiciones a millones de aficionados. Una relación construida sobre el respeto mutuo, la confianza y la cooperación que debemos preservar y seguir fortaleciendo. Nuestro compromiso es seguir trabajando juntos para que un episodio individual no perjudique los importantes avances conseguidos ni afecte a los millones de aficionados chinos que siguen nuestras competiciones. China es y seguirá siendo un socio estratégico para LALIGA

articles.title: El Girona impone su ley
articles.standfirst: Los blanquirrojos demuestran su calidad y efectividad para superar al humilde Cuarte, todo coraje e intensidad
articles.summary: Los blanquirrojos demuestran su calidad y efectividad para superar al humilde Cuarte, todo coraje e intensidad
articles.body: El Girona ganó sin más problemas de los esperados al Cuarte y estará en el sorteo de la segunda eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey (0-2). Los tantos de Abel Ruiz y Pyshchur en cada parte fueron suficientes para que los catalanes controlaran a un equipo de Tercera RFEF que puso intensidad y coraje, aunque con eso no le valió. En la primera parte, el Girona tubo que combatir con un rival intenso, dispuesto a no ponerle las cosas fáciles. El Cuarte avisó primero, pero tímidamente, hasta que los blanquirrojos tomaron el control. Primero Morante remató lamiendo el palo (20') y justo después Abel Ruiz hizo el 0-1 solo en el segundo palo a centro de Lass (23'). Los aragoneses pidieron unas manos de Furtado y forzaron algunos saques de esquina para inquietar a los catalanes, la vía donde se igualan las fuerzas. En el segundo acto, la tónica se mantuvo, con el Cuarte poniendo más corazón que cabeza en el campo y con un Girona que medio sentenció el encuentro con el 0-2 de Pyshchur, que remató en boca de gol un córner que había cabeceado en primera instancia Van de Beek (60'). Los aragoneses intentaron recortar distancias para entrar en el partido y meter un poco de miedo, pero tan sólo inquietaron con un balón colgado que Krapyvtsov no supo atajar primero, pero sí logró reaccionar después a tiro de Vera (69') y un disparo desde fuera del área del mismo lateral zurdo (93').

articles.title: Eze Ponce y Ali Houary evitan un mal trago del Elche en Pinatar
articles.standfirst: Un doblete del argentino y un gol del canterano permiten a los franjiverdes remontar su duelo de Copa
articles.summary: Un doblete del argentino y un gol del canterano permiten a los franjiverdes remontar su duelo de Copa
articles.body: El Elche cumplió ante el Pinatar para avanzar a la segunda ronda de la Copa del Rey. Aunque por un marcador más ajustado de lo que podía presagiarse. Ante un rival cinco categorías inferior, tuvo que remontar para llevarse la contienda por 1-3. Ponce salvó los muebles con un doblete, que volteó la diana inicial de Moha. Y Ali Houary sentenció al borde del final. Más allá del resultado, el partido dejó los debuts oficiales de Iturbe y Lomónaco como franjiverdes. El Pinatar se adelantó en el inicio por medio de Moha, que aprovechó un mal pase atrás de Bigas para superar a Iturbe. El júbilo local duró 14 minutos, hasta que Eze Ponce igualó con un remate en el área pequeña. Tras varias intentonas, el delantero argentino culminó la remontada en el inicio del segundo acto, con un tiro de zurda. El Pinatar echó el resto para buscar la remontada, pero Ali Houary enterró sus esperanzas en la recta final, con un chut ajustado desde fuera del área. Neto y Rubén Sánchez pudieron ampliar la renta visitante, pero el marcador ya no se movió. Ficha técnica Pinatar: Juan Eduardo (Dani Acosta, min 58); Pablo (Riky, min 58), Salva (Hicham, min 68), Tuki, Joseda, Kerru; Vázquez, Iván (Gómez, min 72), Hafid (Pepelu, min 68); Moha y Chipi. Elche: Iturbe; Lomónaco, Barzic, Bigas (Padilla, min 84); Josan (Yago de Santiago, min 62), Neto, Diang (Buonanotte, min 70), Ali Houary, Tete Morente (Rubén Sánchez, min 84); Adam Boayar (Osorio, min 70) y Eze Ponce. Goles: 1-0, Moha (min 18); 1-1, Eze Ponce (min 32); 1-2, Eze Ponce (min 54); 1-3, Ali Houary (min 81). Árbitro: Manuel Jesús Orellana Cid (comité andaluz). Amonestó por parte del Pinatar a Hafid (min 2) y Salva (min 16) y por parte del Elche a Eze Ponce (min 38) y Bigas (min 72). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la primera ronda de la Copa S.M. El Rey disputado en el Estadio José Antonio Perez ante unos 3.000 espectadores.

articles.title: Maryland Offering Free Tuition for Semester in Raffle for Student Attending Illinois Game
articles.summary: Maryland introduced a unique promotion for students attending the team's upcoming football game against Illinois.
articles.body:
Maryland introduced a unique promotion for students attending the team's upcoming football game against Illinois.

Students who stay until the fourth quarter of the contest can enter a raffle for free tuition for the spring 2027 semester, according to Ira Gorawara of The Athletic.

In order to enter the raffle, students must attend Saturday's clash with Illinois at SECU Stadium and scan a QR code shown on the video board before waiting until the fourth quarter.

Maryland's full-time undergraduate tuition for in-state students is $5,507.50 per semester (h/t Gorawara).

The Terrapins have struggled throughout their 2026 campaign, owning a 2-5 record that includes a 0-4 mark in the Big Ten. Since the start of the 2024 season, Maryland has gone a mere 2-20 against conference opponents.

The Terrapins have already made a significant change this year, as head coach Mike Locksley was fired and replaced by interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim on Wednesday.

Maryland will face Illinois on Saturday at 12 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'You are deluded!': Wayne Rooney's scathing attack on Man United players amid Michael Carrick slump
articles.summary: Manchester United are stuck in the middle of a horrible slump which has put manager Michael Carrick's position in serious threat, but according to one club l...
articles.body:
Manchester United are stuck in the middle of a horrible slump which has put manager Michael Carrick's position in serious threat.

They have failed to win any of their last eight games across all competitions, dating back to the 4-0 Champions League victory over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah in mid-September. Starting with the defeat in the subsequent Manchester derby, they have lost five and drawn three by a combined score of 16-6, including 7-1 over their last two games.

Heavy losses to Como and Bournemouth over the past week have put the manager's tenure under heavy pressure, with the club sitting 16th in the Premier League table, and 20th in the Champions League standings.

Carrick has not yet been dismissed, and according to one Man United legend, the players are more to blame than the manager is, and the club will continue to flounder if the squad can't get its act together.

Wayne Rooney says Man United players need a stark reminder

Former Man United star Wayne Rooney is furious with the lack of desire by the players in the current squad, pointing to the recent defeat to Bournemouth as the latest example of what he believes to be poor effort.

"The players haven't got a leg to stand on," Rooney said on the Stick to United podcast which airs on Disney+. "What's not fair is the performances they are giving.

"I looked at the fans, you could see the pain and anger in their faces when those players are walking around the football pitch. You see [Lisandro] Martinez when [Bournemouth forward] Rayan ran round him, they are not getting to the ball, it's so frustrating.

"I could score a goal, had ability or whatever, at least I f***ing ran and put myself about as a team. These players are not doing that. I would love to go in that dressing room and say, 'What the f*** are you all doing? What type of performances do you think this is? Do you think you deserve to wear the shirt?' Put a f***ing firework up their a**** because they are not doing anything.

"We are seeing players who are numb, look like they have got no emotion, look like they don't care. Some of them might care, some good lads who are getting dragged down. It is so frustrating to watch."

Rooney believes that the players have failed to do their part for the team, and therefore are letting the manager down.

"The squad is absolutely a million miles away," Rooney said. "The worst thing for Michael Carrick, he has given the board a bit of hope when in reality, they needed a big overhaul and have done for years.

"The midfield, spending that amount on those midfielders, is absolutely crazy. I feel for Michael, he has being let down, he hasn't been good enough, but the players have let him down massively."

It seems the fans agree with Rooney, at least judging by their cheering and jeering after the Bournemouth defeat on the weekend. The away fans at Vitality Stadium cheered Carrick as he walked down the tunnel, and then began to boo the players once he had disappeared into the underbelly of the stadium.

Michael Carrick to remain as Man United coach for now

According to multiple reports on Tuesday, Manchester United had elected to stick with Michael Carrick for now, despite recent embarrassing defeats to Como and Bournemouth over the past week.

A report from Samuel Luckhurst of The Sun claimed Man United brass had originally planned to sack Carrick, but couldn't agree on a subsequent move forward to replace him, whether interim or permanently, so they decided to stick it out a bit longer.

On Monday, the club had declined to comment whether Carrick would take charge of training on Tuesday, but decided to keep him on for the short-term. According to Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic , the decision came from co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada, and director of football Jason Wilcox. All three executives have also been the target of fan ire in recent weeks as the team flounders.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal’s Reaction Turns Heads After Harry Kane Beats Him for Soccer’s Biggest Award
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal's facial expression became a talking point after Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or, leaving the Barcelona star waiting again. The post Lamine Yamal...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal drew attention for his reaction after Harry Kane was announced as the winner of the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or on Monday, October 26.

Brazilian soccer legend Ronaldo Nazário presented the award to Kane, who became the first Englishman to win the prestigious honor in 25 years.

As the audience rose to applaud the Bayern Munich striker, cameras captured Yamal remaining seated with a serious expression before joining the applause.

The moment quickly circulated on social media, with fans debating whether the 19-year-old was disappointed after missing out on the award for the second consecutive year.

ESPN FC shared the clip on X , writing, "Yamal looking absolutely devastated for the second year in a row as he sees another player take home the Ballon d'Or."

The outlet also highlighted his recent finishes, noting that Yamal placed second in 2025 before dropping to third in 2026.

"The wait goes on for his moment," the post concluded.

Fans React to Lamine Yamal's Expression After Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or Victory

Yamal's reaction drew several responses from soccer fans, many of whom pointed to his age and the opportunities he still has to win the award.

"Mbappe has been waiting for more than 10 years and Harry Kane 15 years if not more. Lamine will definitely win it before 23," one fan commented.

Another wrote, "He's got years to win it yet, sure he'll be fine."

A third fan offered a different perspective on Yamal's third-place finish.

"Finishing third while being the best story in the room most nights is its own kind of trophy," the commenter wrote.

Another supporter referenced the young player's individual accomplishments.

"At this point, with his third time winning it, the Young Talent award just feels insufficient for him and almost as just a way to placate him. He's got next though. Keep your head up, young king."

Harry Kane Wins First Ballon d'Or After Scoring 73 Goals in 65 Matches

Kane defeated Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé and Yamal to claim the award after scoring 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country.

the England captain became the first player from his country to receive the men's Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen won in 2001.

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 matches for Bayern Munich and added six goals for England during the World Cup, where the national team reached the semifinals.

Yamal also entered the ceremony following a successful season.

The Barcelona winger helped Spain win the 2026 World Cup and became the first player under 20 to appear in and win both a European Championship final and a World Cup final.

He also received the award for the world's best young player for the third consecutive season.

Despite his individual recognition and international success, Yamal finished behind Kane and Mbappé in the Ballon d'Or voting.

Lamine Yamal's Uncle Takes Aim at Harry Kane Following Ballon d'Or Results

Yamal's uncle, Abdul Abdellaoui, publicly questioned the voting results and argued that his nephew deserved the award.

Speaking to El Larguero , Abdellaoui expressed disappointment with the decision.

"Well, the truth is it's really sad, I feel really bad," he said.

"My nephew was amazing, he was the best player in the world, everyone knows it. If you like football, you go to see Lamine, not Harry Kane."

Abdellaoui acknowledged Kane's scoring ability but maintained that Yamal offered more on the field.

"Harry Kane is a great goalscorer but Lamine is the best player who shines on the pitch and if he's unlucky, there's next year."

He also suggested that Yamal's age worked against him in the voting.

"Since Lamine is young, they always say he has time, he's 19, and that's why they're not giving him the award. Harry, with only three days of football left, they're saying, 'come on, we'll give him the award'."

Abdellaoui pointed to Yamal's World Cup victory and domestic accomplishments as reasons he believed the teenager should have won.

"He's won the World Cup, La Liga, the Super Cup, he plays really well, he's had an incredible season, he scores goals that nobody else can. Passes, assists, whatever you want."

Despite the criticism, Abdellaoui expressed confidence in his nephew's future.

"Lamine will win more than one, but the sadness will pass in three days. In a few days he will be fine."

Barcelona President Joan Laporta Says Yamal 'Deserved' the Ballon d'Or

Barcelona president Joan Laporta also publicly supported Yamal after the London ceremony.

"I am convinced that he will win the Ballon d'Or, I don't know when, but he deserved it," Laporta said.

He acknowledged that the voting process ultimately determined the winner, despite his belief that Yamal had done enough to earn the honor.

"In my view, he did enough to win the Ballon d'Or, but the voters decided the matter this way, and that must be accepted in a sporting spirit."

Laporta also expressed confidence that the Barcelona squad would support Yamal following the result.

"I hope this will be a motivation for him on a personal level, and I am sure it will be. All his teammates will help him get over this disappointment quickly."

articles.title: ‘Is This a Work?’ ‘I’d Go Back in a Heartbeat’ — Dave Portnoy Makes Feelings Clear on Pat McAfee-Utah Controversy, Asks If ESPN Star Faked Beef
articles.summary: Dave Portnoy apparently left Utah with a very different review than Pat McAfee. With McAfee’s complaints about his “College GameDay” visit turning into a con...
articles.body:
Dave Portnoy apparently left Utah with a very different review than Pat McAfee. With McAfee's complaints about his "College GameDay" visit turning into a controversy, the Barstool Sports founder offered an enthusiastic endorsement of the school. Then he floated another possibility. Was everyone getting worked up?

Dave Portnoy Praises Utah and Questions Pat McAfee's Feud

Portnoy made his feelings about the campus experience clear in a post addressing the controversy.

"With all this Mcafee controversy I just want to say I loved Utah. Granted this was before I became Provo Dave but I loved it. Crowd was great. Fans were great. Id go back in a heartbeat with Barstool Football Show," Portnoy wrote .

His enthusiasm came as McAfee faced backlash over his explanation that he felt uncomfortable at Utah . Portnoy's own experience gave him little reason to join the ESPN personality's complaints about the visit.

In another post, he wondered whether the dispute might have an entertainment angle. "Is this a work? Aren't they going back for the Holy War in 2 weeks?" Portnoy asked .

"Work" is wrestling terminology for something staged. Portnoy was raising that possibility, with a potential return for the Utah-BYU rivalry serving as his punchline. His post offered no evidence that McAfee had manufactured the dispute or that a return visit was confirmed.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Portnoy also expressed surprise in a video shared by another account.

"Utah is awesome. Great environment. Great fans… so that was a little surprising..," Portnoy said in the clip .

That left him with two fairly straightforward positions. He enjoyed Utah, and he was having trouble squaring his experience with the controversy unfolding around McAfee.

McAfee's frustration centered on a video posted by Utah's official Instagram account before Saturday's show. Students mocked him in the video, and he objected to the university distributing it while he was preparing to appear before its audience.

"I've never been more uncomfortable, honestly in my life," McAfee said Monday while explaining his reaction. He also referenced the 2025 killing of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University when discussing his concerns.

ESPN subsequently supported its host. The network said protecting its presenters, production staff, and spectators was a priority and that threats directed at team members warranted serious attention.

"We support Pat and recognize the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security," an ESPN spokeswoman said.

Utah also apologized, accepting responsibility for publishing the video. The school said it had intended a lighthearted post, acknowledged that it had missed the mark, and apologized for creating any perception that McAfee was unsafe or unwelcome.

Those responses treated McAfee's concerns seriously. Portnoy's question about a staged feud remains his speculation.

His offer to return, however, required considerably less interpretation. Whatever McAfee decides about another trip, Portnoy sounds ready to put Utah back on Barstool's itinerary.

articles.title: La Copa asesta la puntilla a Manolo
articles.standfirst: El Espanyol cae eliminado del torneo del KO al ceder ante el Sestao River en la prórroga
articles.summary: El Espanyol cae eliminado del torneo del KO al ceder ante el Sestao River en la prórroga
articles.body: La derrota del Espanyol ante el Sestao River (3-4) en la primera eliminatoria copera bien podría suponer la sentencia para Manolo González, hasta ahora técnico perico. Partido de ida y vuelta que decidió en el último minuto de la prórroga con un tanto de Jon Rojo que hizo justicia a lo visto sobre el verde. Manolo hizo hasta seis cambios respecto a la derrota frente al Racing de Santander, tirando de veteranía, experiencia y compromiso. Aún se estaban asentando ambos equipos sobre un endeble terreno de juego cuando llegó el gol del Espanyol. Marcos Fernández sacó un penalti a favor en un buen juego de espaldas dentro del área, fue el encargado de anotar desde los once metros. Reaccionó el líder del Grupo 1 de la Segunda RFEF con un zurdazo de Castañeda que se fue al lateral de la red. Luego fue Carrión quien recogió un rechace en la medialuna y mandó el balón a las nubes. El premio a la insistencia llegó poco después, cuando el propio Carrión aprovechó un pase entre líneas para zafarse de Hinojo y resolver en el mano a mano con Dmitrovic. El Espanyol, como el bólido que va con neumáticos de seco en un día de lluvia, lo intentó sin suerte ante una defensa local que fue un muro infranqueable. Efremov no se amilanó a pesar de la brecha en la cabeza que se hizo al golpear con un compañero; y Ugarte sumó a su buen hacer defensivo un tanto al borde del descanso al cabecear un córner botado por Delgado. Manolo agitó al avispero en el entreacto dando entrada a Roberto. El ariete tuvo el empate en su primer remate, un balón muerto dentro del área que acabó sacando Efremov en línea de gol. Después remató con el exterior un centro lateral de Hinojo. Otro giro de tuerca con la entrada de Bauzà, Moscardo y Bryan Zaragoza. El Espanyol se volcó en campo contrario y dejó espacios atrás. Uno de ellos lo encontró Bengoetxea para plantarse sólo ante Dmitrivic, pero el guardameta perico salvó el mano a mano. El tramo final se consumió con el campo embarrado, los visitantes colgando balones al área y los locales achicando agua. Sobre la bocina, el árbitro pitó un nuevo penalti a favor del Espanyol por falta de Zearreta sobre Edu Expósito. Lo lanzó Roberto y logró la igualada, llevando así el partido a la prórroga. Si la Copa mola es por partidos de auténtica locura y alternancia como el que disfrutó en Sestao. El Espanyol completó la remontada tras la reanudación con un potente disparo de Moscardo desde la frontal que se coló en la jaula, pero apenas dos minutos después los locales volverían a firmar tablas con un cabezazo de Laka tras una falta botada por Chicharito. Minutos de locura en el tramo final en Las Llanas. Iru salvó a su equipo con un vuelo sin motor ante la chilena de Cabrera y a continuación Dmitrovic sacó un disparo a bocajarro de Markel. En el último minuto, cuando todo el mundo pensaba en la tanda de penaltis, se desató la euforia con el tanto de Rojo, que cazó un balón dividido en el área pequeña para poner la sentencia a un duelo muy copero.
